summary: बुधवार की रात मेरे चचेरे भाई- जो अपनी पत्नी के साथ विदेश में हैं- ने मुझे फोन करके पूछा कि क्या मैं मुंबई में उनके घर जा सकता हूं, ताकि कुछ समय के लिए उनके 13 और 11 साल के बच्चों से मिल सकूं? वायनाड में हुई त्रासदी के बाद से उनका बड़ा बेटा सदमे में था। स्थिति तब और जटिल हो गई, जब वह अपने छोटे भाई को लेकर अचानक बहुत सुरक्षात्मक हो गया। जब बिहार से एक और खबर उसके मोबाइल पर आई कि सुपौल जिले के त्रिवेणीगंज में एक सनसनीखेज घटना में लालपट्टी के एक निजी स्कूल में नर्सरी कक्षा के छात्र ने तीसरी कक्षा में पढ़ने वाले 10 वर्षीय छात्र को गोली मार दी तो उसने उसे स्कूल न जाने की हिदायत दे डाली। बड़े बेटे ने नौकरों को कमरे पर दस्तक देने के बाद ही भीतर आने के निर्देश देना शुरू कर दिया था। चूंकि मैं काम के सिलसिले में महाराष्ट्र के जलगांव में था, इसलिए मेरी पत्नी वहां पहुंचीं और हमने चर्चा की कि इस तरह की त्रासदियों के बारे में बच्चों से कैसे बात की जाए। हम जानते थे कि बच्चों के पास हममें से अधिकतर वयस्कों से ज्यादा जानकारी होती है, लेकिन किसी ने भी उनसे बातचीत शुरू नहीं की थी। इसलिए जब मेरी पत्नी वहां गईं, तो वे दरवाजे की घंटी बजाने के बावजूद बाहर नहीं आए। तभी मेरी पत्नी को अहसास हुआ कि बच्चों को लगता है उनका बंद बेडरूम ही उनका ‘सुरक्षित स्थान’ है। उन्होंने पहले बच्चों को अपनी बात कहने की अनुमति दी। बड़े बेटे ने शुरू किया, ‘आंटी, क्या आपको पता है कि इस देश में एक किंडरगार्टन का बच्चा भी बंदूक लेकर किसी को भी गोली मार सकता है?’ वह कई और बातें कहता रहा, जो सच नहीं थीं। मेरी पत्नी ने शांति से कहा, ‘चूंकि अंकल मीडिया में काम करते हैं, इसलिए क्या हम उनसे उन सभी बातों के बारे में पूछ सकते हैं, जो तुम कह रहे हो? उन्हें बेहतर जानकारी होगी।’ बच्चे सहमत हो गए और मैं उनके साथ ऑनलाइन बातचीत में शामिल हो गया। बाद में मैंने उन्हें सुझाव दिया कि वे एक ड्राइव पर जाएं, क्योंकि मुझे पता था कि कार ड्राइव अक्सर मुश्किल बातचीतों के लिए एक शानदार उपाय होती है, खासकर बच्चों के साथ। क्योंकि आप कमरे में सोफे पर बैठने की तुलना में कार में उनके ज्यादा करीब होते हैं। जब वे डरे हुए महसूस करते हैं तो आप उन्हें गले लगा सकते हैं और चूम सकते हैं। मेरी आवाज कार में लगे रेडियो से जुड़ी हुई थी और मैंने उनसे बात करना शुरू कर दिया। मुझे पता था कि डर आसानी से बढ़ जाता है। जब हम डर पैदा करने वाली बातें सुनते हैं तो हमारा शरीर हमें सुरक्षित रखने के लिए डर की प्रतिक्रियाएं उत्पन्न करता है। यह ठीक वैसा ही है, जैसे किसी कार दुर्घटना के बाद कार में प्रवेश करने का प्रयास करना और हमारे शरीर का हमसे कहना कि ‘मैं अंदर नहीं जा सकता।’ चिंतित बड़े बेटे ने अनुरोध किया कि वह रात को हमारे घर में आकर रहना चाहता है। मुझे पता था कि अगर मैं उसकी चिंता के प्रति सदाशयता जतलाता, तो मैं अनजाने में उसके डर को और मजबूत कर देता। उसे ‘हां’ कहने पर यह सूक्ष्म संदेश जाता कि जब वे अकेले होते हैं तो जोखिम में होते हैं। बड़े बेटे की एंग्जायटी उसे बता रही थी कि ‘उसके और उसके भाई के साथ कुछ भयानक होने वाला है’ और ऐसे में तर्क काम नहीं आता। मैंने उन्हें बताया कि कुछ डर क्यों आधारहीन होते हैं और उनके अनुपातहीन डर पर काबू पाने में उनकी मदद की। पूरी बातचीत के दौरान हमने इस बात पर जोर दिया कि वे सुरक्षित हैं। मेरी पत्नी ने उन्हें सांत्वना देने के लिए कार में उन्हें कसकर पकड़ रखा था। एंग्जायटी की स्थिति में बच्चे आम तौर पर भाग उठते हैं। तब मैंने उन्हें बताया कि जब वास्तव में कोई खतरा न हो, तब भागकर वे कुछ सकारात्मक और मूल्यवान करने का अवसर खो रहे होते हैं। अंततः बच्चों ने कहा कि वे अपने ही घर में सोएंगे, और मेरी पत्नी ने उनसे वादा किया कि वे गुरुवार की सुबह नाश्ते के लिए उन्हें आकर ले जाएंगी। फंडा यह है कि पैरेंट होने का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा यह है कि हम अपने बच्चों की खतरे की स्थिति का सामना करने में किस तरह से मदद करते हैं।

title: संजय कुमार का कॉलम:मध्यम-उच्च मध्यम वर्ग का समर्थन गंवा रही है भाजपा
summary: केंद्रीय बजट के कथित रूप से मध्यम वर्ग विरोधी होने के कारण उसकी आलोचना की जा रही है। इसमें देश के व्यापक मध्यम वर्ग को कोई राहत नहीं दी गई है, जो कि कुल आबादी का लगभग 31% है। ऐसा नहीं है कि अतीत में पेश किए गए बजटों ने मध्यम वर्ग की मांगों और जरूरतों पर बहुत ध्यान दिया हो। लेकिन 2024 के लोकसभा चुनावों में मध्यम वर्ग भाजपा से दूर जाता नजर आया था। यह पार्टी से मध्यम वर्ग के मोहभंग का संकेत था। ऐसे में उम्मीद थी कि बजट इस वर्ग को कुछ सकारात्मक संकेत दे सकता है, जो कि दशकों से भाजपा का कोर-वोटर रहा है। वित्त मंत्री ने मध्यम वर्ग के सामने आने वाली चुनौतियों को तो स्वीकार किया और कर-समायोजन के जरिए राहत प्रदान करने के सरकार के प्रयासों पर जोर भी दिया। लेकिन मध्यम वर्ग के लिए कर एक बड़ी चिंता है। यह याद रखा जाना चाहिए कि यह वर्ग ही सबसे ज्यादा टैक्स देता है। लेकिन दीर्घावधि पूंजीगत लाभ (एलटीसीजी) कर को 10% से बढ़ाकर 12.5% करने और अल्पावधि पूंजीगत लाभ (एसटीसीजी) कर को 15% से बढ़ाकर 20% करने का प्रस्ताव उन लोगों को यकीनन प्रभावित करेगा, जो म्युचुअल फंड और शेयरों में निवेश करते हैं। इससे बड़ी संख्या में मध्यम वर्ग में निवेश के प्रति आकर्षण कम हो जाएगा और उनके संभावित लाभ घट जाएंगे। अपनी संपत्ति बेचने वाले व्यक्तियों के लिए इंडेक्सेशन लाभ को हटाने से भी मध्यम वर्ग के उन लोगों को नुकसान होगा, जो अपना पैसा रियल एस्टेट में लगाते हैं। उलटे इसके परिणामस्वरूप संपत्तियों की बिक्री पर अधिक कर-योग्य लाभ होगा, जिससे मध्यम वर्ग के व्यक्तियों के लिए टैक्स लायबिलिटी बढ़ जाएगी। रिटायरमेंट की प्लानिंग करने वाले या वित्तीय लाभ के लिए संपत्तियां बेचने वालों पर इसका खासा असर हो सकता है। अनुच्छेद 80डी के तहत कटौती की सीमा लगभग एक दशक से स्थिर बनी हुई है। मध्यम वर्ग के परिवार अक्सर अपने पैसों का प्रबंधन करने के लिए कर-कटौती पर निर्भर रहते हैं। उन्हें स्वास्थ्य सेवा पर अधिक खर्च करना पड़ता है, क्योंकि जैसे-जैसे मेडिकल का खर्चा बढ़ता गया है, उस तरह से इस कटौती के लाभ नहीं बढ़े हैं। यह स्थिरता समय के साथ कटौती के वास्तविक मूल्य को कम करती है, जिससे मध्यम वर्ग पर अधिक वित्तीय बोझ पड़ता है। इन तमाम प्रावधानों से मध्यम वर्ग के बीच असंतोष और वित्तीय-तनाव की भावना बढ़ने की संभावना है। उन्हें लग रहा है कि उनके महत्वपूर्ण योगदान और चुनौतियों को पर्याप्त महत्व नहीं दिया गया है। लोकसभा चुनावों में भाजपा को जो नुकसान हुआ, उसमें मध्यम वर्ग की बढ़ती नाराजगी विभिन्न कारणों में से एक है। लोकनीति-सीएसडीएस द्वारा किए गए चुनाव-उपरांत सर्वेक्षण के आंकड़े इस बात की पुष्टि करते हैं कि मध्यम और उच्च मध्यम वर्ग के मतदाताओं की भाजपा से दूरियां बढ़ी हैं। सर्वे के निष्कर्ष बताते हैं कि भाजपा के मध्यम वर्ग के मतदाताओं में 3 प्रतिशत की गिरावट आई है। 2019 में मध्यम वर्ग के 38% लोगों ने भाजपा को वोट दिया था, जो 2024 में घटकर 35% हो गया। हालांकि ये वोट कांग्रेस के खाते में नहीं गए हैं। 2024 में मध्यम वर्ग के 20% लोगों ने कांग्रेस को वोट दिया, जबकि 2019 में यह आंकड़ा 21% था। लेकिन 2024 में मध्यम वर्ग के 3 प्रतिशत अधिक मतदाता इंडिया गठबंधन के पाले में गए। 2019 में यूपीए को इस वर्ग के 29% ही वोट मिले थे। भाजपा को उच्च मध्यम वर्ग के मतदाताओं के बीच भी नुकसान उठाना पड़ा है। 2019 में इस वर्ग के 44% मतदाताओं ने उसे वोट दिया था, जो 2024 में घटकर 41% रह गए। इससे एनडीए का वोट-शेयर भी प्रभावित हुआ। कांग्रेस को 2 प्रतिशत का लाभ हुआ। 2019 में 20% से बढ़कर 2024 में उसे इस वर्ग के 22% वोट मिले। लेकिन इंडिया गठबंधन को बहुत अधिक लाभ हुआ। 2019 में 27% वोटों की तुलना में 2024 में उसे 32% वोट मिले। लोकनीति-सीएसडीएस सर्वेक्षण के निष्कर्ष यह भी बताते हैं कि भाजपा निचले तबके के मतदाताओं के बीच अपना समर्थन बनाए रखने में कामयाब रही है। 2019 में निम्न आय वर्ग के 35% मतदाताओं ने उसे वोट दिया था, जो 2024 में भी कायम रहा। लेकिन पिछले चुनाव की तुलना में इंडिया गठबंधन को निम्न आय वर्ग के मतदाताओं का 7% अधिक समर्थन मिला। 2019 में इस वर्ग के 28% मतदाताओं ने यूपीए को वोट दिया था, जो 2024 में इंडिया गठबंधन के लिए बढ़कर 35% हो गया। निचले तबके के बीच भाजपा की लोकप्रियता में वृद्धि का श्रेय मुफ्त राशन और अन्य कल्याणकारी योजनाओं को जाता है। लेकिन मध्यम और उच्च मध्यम वर्ग के बीच भाजपा के समर्थन-आधार में गिरावट स्पष्ट है। (ये लेखक के अपने विचार हैं)

summary: The Union Ayush ministry declared advertising Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and Homeopathy drugs with "miraculous or supernatural effects" illegal, highlighting the risk to public health from unverified claims. The ministry urged the public to consult registered practitioners before using these drugs and to report any misleading advertisements or false claims. Self-diagnosis and self-medication are strongly discouraged.

title: Delhi BJP leaders expect better show in Delhi Assembly polls after Haryana victory
summary: BJP's unexpected win in Haryana, securing 48 out of 90 seats, is anticipated to influence the forthcoming Delhi elections. BJP plans to highlight Centre's development efforts and welfare schemes, contrasting them with AAP's perceived shortcomings. AAP, despite contesting numerous seats, failed to secure any in Haryana.

title: 'Will support any CM face to ...': Uddhav Thackeray on CM candidate ahead of Maharashtra assembly elections
summary: Uddhav Thackeray reiterates his willingness to support a chief ministerial candidate from Congress or NCP (SP) to save Maharashtra ahead of assembly elections. He criticizes the current Mahayuti government for fake narratives and poor implementation of schemes, emphasizing the importance of justice for native inhabitants.

title: Haryana assembly results: BJP’s Attri claims lowest margin win by 32 votes, Congress’s Patel triumphs with highest of over 98K
summary: The Haryana Assembly elections saw a surprising outcome with BJP securing 48 seats, contrary to exit polls predicting a Congress win. Devender Chatar Bhuj Attri of BJP won Uchana Kalan by 32 votes, while Congress candidate Mamman Khan won Ferozepur Jhirka by 98,441 votes.

title: J&K headed for winter of discontent? It will depend on Lt Guv’s playbook
summary: The J&K LG will have powers similar to the Delhi LG, overseeing key areas including police and prisons. Amendments enhance his control over critical appointments and law enforcement strategies. This might lead to tensions with the elected J&K government, but both parties may need to adapt to these new dynamics in governance.

title: J&K statehood restoration will be top priority, says Congress
summary: The NC-Congress alliance's recent victory is seen as a rejection of BJP's policies and misuse of constitutional power, according to Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge. Congratulating NC leaders, Kharge emphasized the restoration of J&K's statehood as a top priority. The coalition government aims to meet people's aspirations with a transparent, accountable administration.

title: Big win for INDIA bloc fails to hide failure of Congress in Jammu
summary: Despite a strong nationwide performance, Congress falters in Jammu, securing just one seat and failing to challenge BJP's dominance. National Conference's chief criticized Congress for neglecting Jammu, undermining alliance efforts and allowing BJP to capitalize with 29 seats in the region.

title: AAP scores a surprise, finds foothold in J&K
summary: Aam Aadmi Party, expanding its beyond Delhi and Punjab, gained a significant milestone in Jammu and Kashmir by winning the Doda assembly constituency with candidate Mehraj Malik. AAP now has representation in five states, demonstrating its growing influence in Indian politics.

title: Assam extends Afspa in four districts citing 'recent disturbances' in Bangladesh
summary: Afspa has been extended for another six months in Tinsukia, Dibrugarh, Charaideo, and Sivasagar districts of Assam, citing potential security threats from disturbances in Bangladesh. Authorities highlight improvements in Assam's security but express concerns over internal law and order. The controversial act, opposed by human rights groups, grants wide-ranging powers to security forces.

title: Two soldiers abducted by terrorists in J&K's Anantnag, rescue efforts on
summary: In Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, two Territorial Army soldiers were abducted by terrorists in a forest area. One of the soldiers managed to escape. Security forces have launched a search operation to locate and rescue the remaining soldier, as reported by ANI sources.

title: Congress's 'alliance of convenience' comes under fire as Haryana loss wipes out Lok Sabha gains
'Congress joins hands with anti-national forces only to win elections...', says Shehzad Poonawalla
summary: BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla accuses Congress of spreading lies and collaborating with anti-national forces after BJP's victory in Haryana. He criticizes Congress for questioning election results and the integrity of democratic institutions and the Election Commission dismisses Congress's allegations as unfounded.

title: Guinness World Records: Canadian YouTuber Eats More Than 1 Kg Sriracha Hot Sauce In Just 3 Minutes
summary: The speed eater shared that he imagines eating a pumpkin pie while actually gulping down the spicy sauce.

title: BSP will contest assembly elections in Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Delhi: Mayawati
summary: BSP leader Mayawati announced the party's intention to contest assembly elections in Jharkhand, Maharashtra, and Delhi, following their poor performance in Haryana. She attributed the disappointing results to the casteist mentality of the Jat community, despite BSP's alliance with INLD in the polls.

title: 'If arrogance and lack of grace had a face': BJP questions Rahul Gandhi's absence after poll results
summary: BJP IT cell chief Amit Malviya criticises Congress MP Rahul Gandhi for showing arrogance and ingratitude after the party's electoral defeat in Haryana. Malviya accuses Gandhi of not thanking voters and party workers, nor congratulating National Conference leaders on their performance in Kashmir.

title: Odisha Govt transfers funds to 35 lakh women under Subhadra Yojana
summary: Total beneficiaries reach 60 lakh

title: DCA officials conduct raids at quack’s clinic, seize drugs
summary: Acting on a tip-off, the officials discovered that Gurram Sadanandam, falsely claiming to be a rural medical practitioner (RMP), was operating a clinic under the name Suhana First Aid Centre. Drug inspector M. Aravind Kumar led the raid

Odisha: BRM Holds Shastra Pujan, Showcases Self-Defense Skills
summary: Leaders call for national unity and cultural pride

title: Tech for seamless travels: Adani Airports to use Thales’ cloud-based platform
summary: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) partners with Thales to deploy advanced tech solutions at Mumbai, Ahmedabad, and other airports. Thales implements the 'Fly to Gate' biometric system and will soon deploy a cloud-based Airport Operation Control Centre (APOC) to improve airport management and passenger experience significantly. This initiative supports India's vision of becoming the largest aviation market by 2047.

title: Poll strategy in focus as Jharkhand CM Soren meets Kharge, Rahul
summary: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren and his wife met Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi in New Delhi to discuss preparations for the upcoming state assembly polls. Tensions rise within the INDIA bloc post-Haryana election defeat, with Soren opposing the Waqf Amendment Bill 2024.

title: 'Don't think that AAP needs any support': Raghav Chadha says party to go solo in Delhi assembly elections
summary: AAP MP Raghav Chadha expressed confidence in AAP's victory over BJP in the upcoming Delhi assembly elections, stating they don't need support from the INDIA bloc. He categorized elections into two types: those where regional parties like AAP, DMK, and TMC can defeat BJP independently, and those where Congress might need alliance support.

title: 'Usual good smile, but ... ': Congress on what happened inside EC office over Haryana EVM complains
summary: The Congress party submitted complaints to the Election Commission of India regarding alleged discrepancies in 20 assembly constituencies during Haryana elections. Bhupinder Hooda and Pawan Khera cited irregularities in vote counting and machine functionality as reasons for their concerns, seeking a thorough investigation.

title: India clears two mega defence projects for 2 indigenous nuclear submarines & 31 Predator drones
summary: The Indian government has approved a major project to build two nuclear-powered submarines and acquire 31 MQ-9B Predator drones from the US, costing around Rs 68,000 crore, to counter China's regional activities. The submarines and drones will enhance India's intelligence, surveillance, and defensive capabilities.

title: Buy only from Sanatanis, says Akhara Parishad
summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Akhara Parishad has urged Hindus to buy from shops with visible signs of Sanatan Dharma adherence, due to alleged contamination of food and worship items by individuals of a specific religion. ABAP highlights these issues in preparation for Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj.

title: List 'consumer rights violations' by Ola Electric: Govt to ARAI
summary: Ministry of Heavy Industries has asked ARAI to provide details on alleged consumer rights violations by Ola Electric, a beneficiary of government EV incentive schemes. The move follows a notice from CCPA citing over 10,600 complaints, including misleading ads, unfair trade practices, and service delays.

title: Govt study: Rural households' out-of-pocket spend on hospitalisation stay Rs 4,129/yr, urban Rs 5,290
summary: The recent govt survey reveals average out-of-pocket medical expenses for hospitalisation in rural and urban areas at Rs 4,129 and Rs 5,290, respectively. Non-hospitalisation costs are Rs 539 and Rs 606. Literacy and numeracy rates are high in the 15-24 age group, while 23.3% are not in education, employment, or training. Most households have a telephone or mobile connection.

title: Star Health CISO leaked customer data, says hacker
summary: The CISO of Star Health Insurance is accused by a hacker named xenZen of being behind a massive customer data breach via API access. UK-based researcher Jason Parker confirmed the authenticity of the hacker's claims. Star Health is investigating and has sought an injunction to prevent data access.

title: Statehood resolution to be passed in 1st cabinet meet: Omar Abdullah
summary: Omar Abdullah, vice president of National Conference, declared that the new government would immediately pass a resolution for restoring J&K's statehood, urging the Prime Minister to act on this promise. He also acknowledged Article 370's complexities, urging future engagement. Coalition discussions with PDP are not prioritized. His son Zamir criticized Center's alleged strategies to undermine NC.

title: Congress seeks probe; Election Commission states, party rejecting will of people
summary: After Congress rejected the Haryana election results as 'unexpected and unacceptable,' party leaders met with the Election Commission (EC) demanding a thorough investigation. The EC criticized Congress spokespersons Jairam Ramesh and Pawan Khera for allegedly undermining democratic principles while acknowledging complaints about EVM issues.

title: AAP alliance could've helped Congress in Haryana, but just to boost its tally by 3
summary: The absence of a Congress-AAP alliance in the Haryana assembly elections likely did not cost Congress the victory. Only in three of the 53 contested seats did AAP's votes exceed the winning margins, potentially adding just three more seats to Congress's tally.

title: NC unlikely to reverse 10% ST quota for Paharis in J&K
summary: The National Conference sources indicated that reversing the 10% ST reservation for the Pahari community in Jammu and Kashmir is unlikely, fearing agitations. They argue that changes might spark protests, affecting the new government. BJP's failure to win in Pahari-populated areas further complicates the situation.

title: Naya Kashmir? BJP's Jammu confinement reeks of the old
summary: The National Conference-Congress alliance won the Kashmir region, seen as a rejection of the BJP's policies post-2019. The BJP's strategy to use proxies in Kashmir failed, leading to a significant setback. While the BJP maintained a hold in Jammu, the results indicate dissatisfaction with changes in Kashmir's status.

title: An unlikely Insta sensation who beat many an influencer
summary: Ratan Tata, with millions of followers on X and Instagram, emerged as an unexpected social media star. Known for his nostalgic posts, messages of empathy, and personal reflections, Tata’s social media presence has evolved into a platform for support amidst false claims and widespread admiration.

title: Ratan Tata the artiste & his collaborative painting at Mumbai’s Taj Mahal Palace
summary: In 2006, Ratan Tata collaborated with painter Lakshman Shrestha to create an artwork for a charity auction, dedicating several days to learning and painting. The artwork, valued at Rs 75 Lakh, now holds a prominent place in Mumbai’s Taj Mahal Palace lobby, contributing significantly to the funds raised.

title: Second major drug bust in Delhi this week: Police seize 200 kg of cocaine worth Rs 2,000 crore
summary: Law enforcement officials in Delhi seized 200 kg of cocaine worth Rs 2,000 crore in a significant drug bust, marking the second largest seizure within a week. Ongoing raids continue to target suspects as part of the larger investigation into a previous Rs 5,620 crore drug haul.

Mathu Vadalara 2 OTT Release Date Confirmed

Study indicates significant shale gas generation potential in Jharkhand
summary: A new study by the Birbal Sahni institute of Palaeosciences reveals significant shale gas potential in the South Karanpura coalfield of Jharkhand. The research suggests favourable conditions for hydrocarbon preservation, contributing to future energy resource development and national energy security, underlining the crucial role of unconventional resources.

title: British woman on death row, 27 Muslim inmates participate in Navratri fast and rituals
summary: A group of 27 Muslim inmates and a British woman on death row at New Delhi's district jail are observing the nine-day Navratri fast, participating in traditional prayers and a havan. The jail administration has supported them with essentials such as boiled potatoes, milk, fruits, and puja materials.

title: John Abraham's Vedaa gets an OTT Release Date
PM Modi-led govt ended policy paralysis of UPA regime: Amit Shah
summary: Home Minister Amit Shah highlighted the Modi government's achievements over the past decade, transforming India's economy from high inflation to robust growth, improving global rankings, and eradicating corruption. He urged industries to scale globally, emphasizing India's future dominance in manufacturing, technology, and infrastructure.

title: RG Kar case: Bengal governor, Kolkata police expresses concern over deteriorating health of protesting doctors
summary: West Bengal Governor CV Ananda Bose addresses junior doctors' hunger strike over the tragic rape-murder of a medic at RG Kar Medical College. Bose promises to hold a peace meeting with stakeholders to resolve the crisis and urges the doctors to end their fast while continuing their protest safely. Key demands include better hospital security and improved healthcare facilities.

title: What pulled down BJP in Pir Panjal
summary: BJP faced a tough defeat in Pir Panjal region, securing only one of eight assembly seats in Rajouri and Poonch, attributed to political dynamics post-abrogation of Article 370, polarisation over the Pahari quota row, and rising terrorist activities. National Conference and Congress dominated the remaining seats.

title: National Conference 'CM-elect' Omar to stake claim 'in a day or two', 4 Independents back alliance
summary: Omar Abdullah of the National Conference is set to stake his claim to form Jammu & Kashmir's first elected government since its union territory status, with support from 49 MLAs, including Congress. The decision follows a crucial party meeting and amidst concerns of potential defections reminiscent of past political upheavals. Congress's weakened position remains a focal point.

title: 8 railway services notified as sub cadre under IRMS
summary: The railway board has announced eight streams under the Indian Railway Management Service, dividing recruitment between Civil Services Exam and Engineering Services Exam. This change aims to balance the need for both technical and non-technical personnel, with a total IRMS cadre strength set at 8,458.

title: Liquor smugglers attack cops in Bihar; sub-inspector injured
summary: Liquor smugglers in Bihar assaulted a police team sent to arrest a wanted criminal in Katihar district, critically injuring a sub-inspector. The attackers attempted to snatch police rifles, forcing the team to retreat. Raids are ongoing to apprehend those involved.

title: In anger at Canada minister’s remarks, Pannun threatens to ‘Balkanise India’
summary: Gurpatwant Singh Pannun of SFJ, designated as a terrorist by India, releases a video threatening to initiate independence movements in multiple Indian states and claims Arunachal Pradesh for China. He vows to use Canadian and American laws to destabilize India by 2047.

title: Congress reviews Haryana loss, to pause EVM attack till it has ‘enough evidence’
summary: After its Haryana election loss, Congress shifts focus from blaming EVMs to addressing internal factional feuds and weaknesses. Congress chief Kharge held a review meeting, deciding to investigate EVM discrepancies with a technical team. Key figures like Hooda and Selja were excluded to avoid bad optics. Rahul Gandhi emphasized party unity for future success.

title: Asean friendship crucial in times of conflict: PM Modi
summary: India and ASEAN emphasize mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity amid maritime disputes, with PM Modi proposing initiatives for enhanced connectivity. Leaders highlight the role of Unclos and call for a substantive South China Sea Code of Conduct to ensure regional peace and stability.

title: Law catches up with love: 27 years on, man arrested for ‘kidnapping’ wife
summary: A 48-year-old grandfather was unexpectedly arrested for allegedly kidnapping his wife 27 years ago. Despite living happily with four daughters and two grandchildren, the outdated charges resurfaced when police in Mehsana recognized him, leading to his brief incarceration before being granted bail.

title: ED slaps Rs 2,100 crore fine on NBFC for loan app with Chinese links
summary: Hyderabad's Enforcement Directorate has imposed a Rs 2,146 crore penalty on PC Financial Services for Fema violations linked to Chinese and Norwegian entities. The NBFC ran a loan app called 'CashBean'. The investigation revealed fraudulent remittances and usurious interest rates, leading to the cancellation of its registration by the RBI and property seizures worth Rs 252 crore in India.

title: Aid to minority body & salaries of madrassa teachers increased by Maharashtra cabinet
summary: The Maharashtra state cabinet increased the share capital of the Maulana Azad Minorities Financial Development Corporation to Rs 1,000 crore and raised the loan guarantee to Rs 500 crore. Additionally, the salaries for contracted B Ed and D Ed teachers in madrassas were significantly increased.

title: PM Modi holds talks with new Japan PM to bolster defence & trade ties
summary: PM Modi and newly appointed Japanese counterpart Shigeru Ishiba reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen India-Japan strategic partnership through enhanced trade, defense, and cultural cooperation at the Asean-India Summit. They emphasized their indispensable partnership for a peaceful Indo-Pacific region.

title: Muslim outfit to fight civic court order to raze Shimla mosque
summary: The All-Himachal Muslims' Organisation (AHMO) plans to contest the Shimla municipal court's order mandating the demolition of the top three floors of Sanjauli mosque, asserting that the agreement given by some individuals does not reflect the community's stance. Concurrently, a campaign promoting economic boycott of Muslim vendors emerges.

title: Kerala House okays resolution urging Centre to junk one nation one election plan
summary: The Kerala assembly passed a resolution urging the central government to reverse its approval of the 'one nation, one election' proposal recommended by the Ramnath Kovind panel. Labeling the decision as undemocratic and unconstitutional, the resolution highlights concerns about weakening federalism and cutting short terms of state assemblies and local self-governments.

title: Bhole Baba appears before judicial panel in stampede case
summary: Surajpal, known as Bhole Baba, was questioned by a judicial panel regarding the July 2 stampede in Hathras that resulted in 121 deaths. Bhole Baba submitted affidavits from attendees to clarify events. His lawyer AP Singh stated that the SIT and the commission have cleared Baba of any wrongdoing, implicating Rajesh Yadav instead.

title: SP-Congress alliance for UP bypolls intact: Akhilesh Yadav
summary: SP president Akhilesh Yadav confirmed the continuation of his party's alliance with Congress for the upcoming bypolls in 10 Uttar Pradesh assembly seats despite recent speculations of a rift. Of the seats, SP held five, BJP three, and one each by RLD and Nishad Party.

title: Speed up Wayanad relief measures, HC tells Centre
Probe 2 contradictory orders posted on court website: Allahabad high court
summary: The Allahabad high court directed an investigation by the Ghaziabad district judge into how two contradictory orders were uploaded in a defamation case, one of which was unsigned. A young magistrate involved apologized for the error, citing it was unintentional.

title: Action, not charges, key to suicide abetment: Supreme Court
summary: The Supreme Court has discharged three Hindustan Unilever Ltd officials charged with abetment of suicide, ruling that mere harassment allegations are insufficient without clear evidence of direct and alarming incitement leading to the act. The court emphasized the need for intention to compel suicide to be prima facie established.

title: Hours after arrest, 1 of 2 Surat rape accused dies in custody
summary: A 45-year-old accused in the gang rape of a teenager in Surat died in police custody after falling ill. Arrested alongside another suspect, he was transferred to a hospital after complaining of breathlessness but succumbed during treatment. The incident unraveled when the duo attacked the victim and her friend, leading to a swift police operation for their capture.

One junior doctor on fast admitted to hospital after his condition worsened
summary: One of the hunger-striking medics, Aniket Mahato, was hospitalised due to deteriorating health conditions. The seven doctors have been fasting for five days, demanding justice for a rape and murder victim at RG Kar Hospital. A team of specialists evaluated their health, urging hospitalisation as a precautionary measure.

title: Akhilesh Yadav visits JPNIC in night, slams government for barring entrance with tin sheets
summary: Akhilesh Yadav criticized the Yogi Adityanath government for obstructing the Jayaprakash Narayan International Centre's main gate with tin sheets on the socialist leader's birth anniversary. Yadav linked this action to the BJP's disdain for freedom fighters and accused them of hindering democracy.

title: 'Enhancing Connectivity and Resilience': PM Modi unveils 10-point plan to boost ASEAN-India ties
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled a 10-point plan to bolster the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Partnership at the 21st ASEAN-India Summit to enhance connectivity and resilience.

title: PM Modi meets US secretary of state Antony Blinken on sidelines of East Asia Summit, condoles lives lost in Hurricane Milton
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the adverse impact of global conflicts on the Global South at the 19th East Asia Summit, calling for peace and stability in Eurasia and West Asia. Simultaneously, US Secretary of State Antony Blinken expressed concerns over China's actions in the South China Sea during the US-ASEAN summit.

summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Laos for the 21st ASEAN-India and 19th East Asia Summit strengthened India's commitment to ASEAN relations. He also engaged in bilateral meetings and discussed challenges in the Indo-Pacific region.

summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court's Indore bench has raised concerns about the deteriorating state of police storerooms (malkhanas) after evidence in a case was damaged by rats. Justice Subodh Abhyankar has directed the police to improve malkhana conditions and regularly update inventories to prevent future incidents.

summary: India's industrial output fell 0.1% in August due to declines in mining and power generation sectors, down from 4.7% growth in July

title: Dussehra 2024: President Murmu and PM Modi to attend grand Ramlila finale
summary: This Dussehra, Delhi's Ramlilas promise a grand finale with the President and Prime Minister attending the Ram-Ravan battle at Shri Dharmik Leela Committee's pandal in Red Fort's Madhavdas Park. summary: RSS chief speak out against woke and cultural Marxists

summary: The West Bengal government has dismissed the mass resignation letters from senior doctors as legally invalid, amid widespread protests supporting junior doctors demanding justice for a colleague's murder and improved workplace security. State-run hospital services remain unaffected as senior doctors fulfill their duties.

title: Congress suspends MLA Sulbha Khodke for 'anti-party activities'
summary: Maharashtra Congress has suspended Sulbha Khodke, Amravati MLA, for six years due to her dissent, including cross-voting against the party in legislative council elections, leading to Jayant Patil’s defeat. State chief Nana Patole confirmed the decision, citing Khodke’s continuous anti-party activities. Sources suggest Khodke may join Ajit Pawar's faction of the NCP.

title: 'List of 20 seats sent to EC ...': Congress raises concerns over credibility of EVMs
summary: Congress has raised concerns over the credibility of EVMs used in Haryana polls, highlighting a suspicious pattern where machines with 99% battery charge led to losses for Congress candidates. A list of 20 such seats has been submitted to the Election Commission for investigation.

title: 'Dedication to Maa Bharati inspirational': PM Modi congratulates RSS on 100th foundation day
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulates RSS as it celebrates its 100th foundation day, highlighting its role in India's development. He encourages listening to RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat's speech, where Bhagwat condemns violence against Hindus in Bangladesh and speaks on Vijayadashami.

title: 'BJP party of terrorists': Mallikarjun Kharge responds to PM Modi's 'Urban Naxals' remark
summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized BJP, calling it a 'party of terrorists' following PM Modi's remark about Congress being taken over by Urban Naxals. Kharge accused BJP of supporting violence against scheduled castes and tribes, including lynching, rape, and other atrocities.

title: RSS' 100th Foundation Day: Full text of speech by Mohan Bhagwat
summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat asserted that India has gained global respect and strength but is facing destabilization attempts. Speaking at the Vijayadasahmi rally, he highlighted the importance of national character and vigilance against conspiracies. Bhagwat also emphasized the need for harmony, values, and self-reliance to counter challenges and maintain unity.

title: Bengal government clarified doctors mass resignations- infructuous
summary: The Bengal government declared that mass resignations by medical college faculties lack legal validity, emphasizing that resignation is an individual matter between the employer and employee. Despite various resignations being submitted, they need to conform to service rules for acceptance. The state also highlighted safety measures implemented in hospitals.

title: BSF foils infiltration bid of Bangladeshis in Tripura
summary: BSF troops in South Tripura apprehended nine Bangladeshi nationals attempting border crossings, including one with 3600 Taka and Rs 3000. Additional operations in North Tripura and a coordinated effort at Agartala railway station led to more detentions. All detainees hail from Chattogram, Dhaka, and Cumilla in Bangladesh.

title: Former Delhi University professor GN Sai Baba passed away
summary: Former Delhi University professor GN Sai Baba passed away on Saturday at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Science (NIMS) hospital due to post-surgery complications. Sai Baba, who previously faced accusations of links with CPI Maoists and was acquitted in March 2024, developed complications after gallbladder surgery last month.

title: Ex-Delhi University professor GN Saibaba passes away
summary: Former Delhi University professor GN Sai Baba, previously accused of links with banned Maoist groups and incarcerated in Nagpur Central Jail, passed away at NIMS hospital. Sai Baba, arrested in 2014 and later acquitted, was released after Bombay high court's decision.

title: Who was Baba Siddique? NCP leader shot dead in Mumbai
summary: Baba Siddique, seasoned politician from Mumbai and long-time member of the Indian National Congress, was slain in a shooting near his son's office in Bandra East. Known for his contributions to urban development, his death is under investigation with two suspects in custody.

title: Sena vs Sena: Dusshera rallies in Mumbai turn political as Shinde, Uddhav take aim at each other
summary: CM Eknath Shinde and Uddhav Thackeray's Dusshera rallies escalate Maharashtra election tension. Shinde defends his split from Shiv Sena, credits PM Modi for Marathi's classical status, and counters Thackeray’s Dharavi redevelopment project claims, promising improved housing. ​Thackery also spoke on PM Modi visiting Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud's house for aarti on the occasion of the Ganesh festival.

title: 'Security of peacekeepers of paramount importance': India on Israel-Lebanon conflict

title: Government portal for internships now open for Prime Minister Internship Scheme
summary: The Prime Minister Internship Scheme has opened applications for candidates aged 21-24. Starting December 2, the scheme offers year-long internships in India's top 500 companies, with candidates receiving financial aid. The portal now features 80,000 opportunities across various sectors, including energy and hospitality.

title: Gym owner murder: Sharpshooter arrested after encounter with police in Delhi

title: 'Omar Abdullah stand on swearing-in will delay J&K's statehood': Engineer Rashid
summary: Engineer Rashid criticizes CM-to-be Omar Abdullah for ignoring his advice on delaying oath-taking until statehood is restored in J&K, which he believes could have expedited the process. Despite Rashid's party winning only one seat, he remains a significant political figure arguing his stance isn't anti-national.

title: Government rolls out PM internship portal, 190+ firms offer 90,000 opportunities
summary: The portal for registration for the PM Internship scheme is now live, providing over 90,000 internship opportunities in 190 companies to enhance employability among youth aged 21-24. With a monthly allowance and one-time grant, this pilot project aims to bridge the skill gap and improve job prospects.

title: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat: Hindus must take lessons from Bangladesh violence
summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat emphasizes the need for Hindu unity and strength to protect against atrocities, citing persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh. He calls for organized societal efforts and warns against violence and fanaticism, urging a national narrative against cultural Marxism while adhering to democratic principles.

title: Ramdas Athawale ready for VBA merger under Ambedkar kin's leadership
summary: Union minister Ramdas Athawale is willing to merge his party, RPI(A), with Vanchit Bahujan Aaghadi and work under Prakash Ambedkar's leadership. The court, hearing the leader's anticipatory bail plea, acknowledged her right to free speech but expressed disapproval of her social media post, terming it as containing "unwarranted insinuations" against a religious community.

title: HC cites lack of proof, junks sedition, extortion FIRs against IPS officer
summary: The Chhattisgarh High Court dismissed three FIRs against IPS officer G P Singh. The court found the FIRs, which included charges of sedition, extortion, and disproportionate assets, to be baseless. The court determined that the FIRs lacked evidence and appeared to be intended for harassment. Singh, an ADGP at the time of the FIRs, was cleared of all charges.

title: High court voids Himachal’s appointment of 6 parliamentary secretaries
summary: The Himachal Pradesh High Court deemed the appointment of six Congress MLAs as chief parliamentary secretaries unconstitutional. The court declared the appointments void and ordered the immediate withdrawal of all privileges and facilities, stating the appointments were outside the legislative authority of the state assembly.

title: SC slams bulldozer brakes, but it comes too late for many
summary: In Uttar Pradesh, authorities demolished multiple homes following a gunfight, dacoity, and Muharram clashes, leaving families homeless and struggling. Victims recount the trauma of losing their homes and possessions, with some forced to leave their town and children's educations disrupted. They question the justice of being punished for the alleged crimes of family members.

title: Fix creamy layer criteria without delay, say MPs
summary: A parliamentary panel met to discuss the "creamy layer" issue for OBC reservations. The panel raised concerns about the delay in revising the income ceiling for OBC reservations. The current ceiling of Rs 8 lakh was set in 2017 and is due for revision. The panel urged the government to expedite the revision process.

title: Stones & sticks fly as Sena factions clash in Mumbai
summary: Supporters of the Shiv Sena and the Shiv Sena (UBT) clashed violently outside Matoshree Club in Mumbai on Tuesday night. The clash, which lasted for an hour, was sparked by allegations of money distribution inside the club. Both sides have filed FIRs against each other, accusing the other of assault, molestation, and intimidation.

title: 3 held for threatening and robbery
Throw out Congress, save ‘roti, beti & maati’: PM Modi in Jharkhand
summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi campaigned in Santhal Pargana for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the Jharkhand assembly elections. Modi urged voters to support the BJP to protect their land, livelihoods, and daughters. He accused the Congress party of opposing reservation policies and encouraging demographic changes in Jharkhand that threaten tribal communities.

title: A vintage Rolls-Royce that wrecked a royal marriage
summary: A vintage Rolls-Royce car, once owned by the Maharani of Baroda, is at the center of a dowry dispute. The car was ordered by Jawaharlal Nehru. The dispute involves the daughter of a Gwalior royal family and a man from a family running an educational institution. The marriage ended shortly after the ceremony.

97 govt schools in Sikkim to be shut due to shortage of students
summary: The Sikkim government announced the closure of 97 schools with low enrollment. Education Minister Raju Basnet stated that students will be merged into nearby schools to improve resource allocation and educational quality. This decision aligns with the government's commitment to prioritize education.

title: India successfully test-fires guided Pinaka weapon system
summary: India successfully conducted flight tests of the Guided Pinaka Weapon System, meeting the required standards for range, accuracy, and rate of fire. The tests involved firing rockets from upgraded Pinaka launchers, demonstrating the system's ability to engage multiple targets. This indigenous system, developed by DRDO and other agencies, enhances the artillery firepower of the Indian Army.

title: Grand Hyatt Mumbai's China House Restaurant Offers A Divine Dim Sum Experience
summary: Chef Yajun Zhang, who has been with the restaurant since its inception 18 years ago, is the force behind its delightful dim sums and other signature dishes.

NIA attaches property of terrorist arrested for killing 2 migrant workers in Kashmir
summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) attached property belonging to Adil Manzoor Langoo, a key suspect in the February killing of two migrant workers in Srinagar. Langoo, linked to the Lashkar-e-Taiba offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF), was arrested with two others. The NIA alleges the killings were part of a larger conspiracy to spread terror, orchestrated by their Pakistan-based handler.

title: Adani hosted 2019 talks but he wasn’t part of it: Sharad Pawar
summary: Sharad Pawar confirmed a 2019 meeting at Gautam Adani's residence. Amit Shah and Ajit Pawar were present for power-sharing discussions between BJP and NCP. Ajit Pawar stated the meeting involved talks of BJP dropping cases against NCP leaders in exchange for joining forces. Sharad Pawar expressed reservations, leading to the collapse of the short-lived government.

title: Panel to discuss again whether to factor in 'salary' to determine 'creamy layer'
summary: A parliamentary committee, revisiting a long-standing debate, is set to discuss the inclusion of "salary" in determining the "creamy layer" for OBC reservation in UPSC exams. MPs argue that including "salary" contradicts a 1993 order, while the government justifies its stance based on the lack of "equivalence of posts" between PSU and government jobs.

title: 3 people are killed in random stabbings in New York City. A suspect is in custody
Dominica to honour PM for aid during pandemic
summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to receive Dominica's highest civilian award, the Dominica Award of Honour. The award recognizes Modi's contributions to Dominica during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly the supply of 70,000 AstraZeneca vaccine doses in 2021.

title: ED mounts searches on 20 premises tied to top poll bond buyer
summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at 20 locations linked to Santiago Martin, a significant political donor known as the 'lottery king,' and his associates. The searches, spanning across multiple states, are part of an ongoing investigation into alleged money laundering related to the illegal distribution and sale of lotteries.

title: Adani wasn't part of 2019 talks but Pawar was, and he betrayed us: Fadnavis
summary: Maharashtra Deputy CM Devendra Fadnavis clarified that businessman Gautam Adani was not present at the 2019 BJP-NCP meeting, contrary to Ajit Pawar's claims. Fadnavis asserted that Sharad Pawar, who was present, later betrayed their agreement on government formation. He also indicated the possibility of imposing President's Rule was discussed, with Sharad Pawar tasked to write to the Governor.

title: JMM-Congress’s ‘jihad welfare’ altering J’khand demography: Anurag Thakur
summary: Anurag Thakur, Former Union Minister, has accused the JMM-Congress-RJD government in Jharkhand of promoting "love jihad" and "land jihad," leading to demographic shifts. He alleged that the government prioritizes appeasement politics over tribal rights and public welfare. Thakur criticized the government's failure to fulfill promises regarding employment, benefits, and tribal welfare, citing corruption and unfulfilled promises as evidence of misgovernance.

title: Dalit houses torched, Ambedkar statue desecrated in MP
summary: A Dalit colony in Madhya Pradesh's Gohta village was attacked by a mob following polling, resulting in four houses being set ablaze and a statue of B.R. Ambedkar vandalized. While locals reported the incident to police, authorities claimed no formal complaint was lodged and downplayed the event as common election-related tension.

title: Congress seeks EC action against PM, Shah for ‘poll code violations’
summary: The Congress party has filed a complaint with the Election Commission against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, alleging that they made divisive and false statements during election rallies in Maharashtra and Jharkhand. The Congress is seeking an immediate ban on campaigning by both leaders.

title: UP woman arrested for killing father to foil his bid to sell family land
summary: A 20-year-old woman in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, has been arrested for the murder of her father. Initially thought to be a natural death, a postmortem revealed that Satyawan Singh had been strangled. Police investigations revealed inconsistencies in the daughter's account, leading to her confession.

title: Funding hiked, social science research to get major push
summary: The Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR) has announced expanded funding for social science research, with a budget of Rs 235 crore. Key initiatives include studies on vulnerable tribal groups, support for women researchers, and research projects for undergraduate and postgraduate students. These initiatives aim to promote inclusivity and address critical social issues.

title: Invaders & colonisers ruined our science for 1,ooo yrs: Infosys founder
summary: Infosys founder NR Narayana Murthy called for India to reclaim its historical leadership in science and innovation. He argued that invasions and colonization stifled Indian science for centuries, hindering critical thinking and innovation among youth. Murthy believes that reviving STEM fields is crucial for solving the nation's problems.

title: Cop demands Rs 30 lakh dowry, bride walks out of wedding
summary: A police constable in Agra was arrested for demanding a dowry of Rs 30 lakh from his bride's family on their wedding day. The bride bravely refused to marry him, leading to his arrest and subsequent release on bail. The incident highlights the persistent issue of dowry demands in India, even among those tasked with upholding the law.

title: Eye banks that don’t collect 100 corneas a year can lose licence
summary: The Indian government has issued a directive mandating that eye banks collect a minimum of 100 corneas annually to retain their operating licenses. This decision, aimed at addressing the issue of underperforming eye banks, could impact the accessibility of corneal transplants for individuals with vision loss due to corneal damage.

title: SC stays Jharkhand HC order for CBI probe into job scam in House
summary: The Supreme Court has halted a Jharkhand High Court order for a CBI investigation into an alleged assembly recruitment scam. The court admitted the assembly secretariat's plea challenging the order's legality. The High Court had mandated the probe due to alleged non-cooperation from the secretariat in addressing the alleged irregularities.

title: Land of Jharkhand irrigated by sacrifices of tribals: PM on state's foundation day
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended his greetings to the people of Jharkhand on the state's foundation day, acknowledging the sacrifices of the tribal community. He highlighted the state's rich natural resources and expressed his hope for its rapid development. Jharkhand, carved out of Bihar, celebrates its foundation day on Birsa Munda's birth anniversary, a revered tribal freedom fighter.

title: Indian students protest outside Oxford Union over debate on Kashmir
summary: Indian students gathered in protest outside the Oxford Union in the UK on Thursday, expressing their disapproval of a debate centered on Kashmiri independence. The debate, organized by the Oxford Union, featured panelists both for and against the motion, sparking controversy over the selection of speakers and the sensitive nature of the topic.

title: Cash-starved civic bodies struggle to take up public works; generate only 32% revenue from own sources: CAG
summary: A series of audits by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) have revealed that urban local bodies (ULBs) across India are grappling with financial instability, generating only a third of their revenue independently and relying heavily on state and central funding.

title: ‘When seen from space, there’s a sense that Earth is everything we have’: Booker winner
summary: In a conversation about her Booker Prize-winning novel 'Orbital,' author Samantha Harvey delved into the process of depicting Earth from the perspective of astronauts aboard the International Space Station. She highlighted the awe-inspiring beauty and fragility of our planet when viewed from space, emphasizing the importance of protecting our home.

summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX envisions revolutionizing travel with its Starship, aiming to transport passengers between global cities in under an hour. The spacecraft would travel 'parallel' to Earth's surface, potentially enabling journeys from New York to Shanghai in 39 minutes.

title: Man suffers 'heart attack' on Delhi-Mumbai flight; doctor onboard saves his life
summary: A doctor traveling on an IndiGo flight from Delhi to Mumbai successfully assisted a passenger experiencing a suspected heart attack. The doctor, Prashant Bharadwaj, responded to a call for help and provided medical attention, stabilizing the passenger's condition before the flight's safe landing in Mumbai.

title: NIA arrests Mohammed Ali Jinnah in Tamil Nadu Ramalingam murder case linked to PFI
summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) apprehended M Mohammed Ali Jinnah in Tamil Nadu for providing refuge to a fugitive involved in the 2019 murder of Ramalingam. Ramalingam was killed by members of the banned outfit Popular Front of India (PFI) for opposing their conversion activities.

The conference showcased research aligned with Indian knowledge systems and future technologies.

summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has filed a supplementary chargesheet against Solomona, a key accused in an illegal arms and ammunition supply case. summary: Devendra Fadnavis, Maharashtra's Deputy Chief Minister, accused the Maha Vikas Aghadi of pursuing a "vote jihad" by appealing to religious sentiments for electoral gain. Fadnavis urged a "dharma-yudh of votes" to counter this alleged tactic, citing the MVA's reported written assurances to the Ulema Council, including demands for Muslim reservations and the release of 2012 riot accused.

title: 700 kg of meth worth Rs 3,000 crore seized from boat off Gujarat coast
summary: Narcotics Control Bureau, Delhi, Indian Navy and Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad seized a massive 700 kg of methamphetamine, worth up to Rs 3,500 crore, from a foreign boat off the Porbandar coast. Eight suspected Iranian nationals were arrested. In a separate operation in Delhi, 82.5 kg of cocaine, valued at Rs 900 crore, was seized.

title: Mutton mayhem: BJP MP's feast turns chaotic over missing meat
summary: A feast organized by BJP MP Vinod Kumar Bind in Mirzapur turned chaotic when guests were allegedly served mutton gravy without any meat. The incident escalated into a physical altercation, forcing attendees to leave. While Bind remained unavailable for comment, his representative claimed the disruption was caused by intoxicated youths who were not invited to the event.

title: Manipur protests intensify over killing of 10 'militants'
summary: Hundreds protested in Churachandpur, demanding justice for the 10 "armed militants" killed in the Nov 11 Jiribam gunfight. Kuki-Zo groups allege the deceased were "volunteers" protecting villages from valley-based attackers. They cite the alleged rape and murder of a woman at Zairawn on November 7 as evidence of the threat.

title: India welcomes Sri Lanka president mandate, reiterates invitation
summary: President Anura Dissanayake's leftist coalition secured a landslide victory in Sri Lanka's parliamentary election. India welcomed the outcome and reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral ties. Indian High Commissioner Santosh Jha extended an invitation for Dissanayake to visit India, emphasizing the importance of cooperation and mutual benefit.

title: At tribal heartland, Rahul Gandhi again flashes his red book, vows to hold caste census
summary: Addressing a rally in Jharkhand, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP and RSS of trying to "kill" the Constitution by dividing the nation along caste and communal lines. He promised a caste census and increased reservations for OBCs, STs, and SCs if the INDIA bloc comes to power in the state.

title: Denied ticket, JMM’s Littipara MLA Dinesh William Marandi joins BJP
summary: Jharkhand Mukti Morcha MLA Dinesh William Marandi joined the BJP after being denied a ticket by his party. Marandi accused the JMM leadership of threats and expressed his commitment to Jharkhand's progress. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan welcomed him and criticized the Hemant Soren government for corruption and poor governance.

After Ajit Pawar, BJP netas too oppose 'Batenge toh...' slogan
summary: UP CM Yogi Adityanath's controversial "Batenge toh katenge" slogan has sparked criticism from within the BJP's Maharashtra alliance. Prominent BJP figures, including Pankaja Munde and Ashok Chavan, expressed reservations, while NCP leaders also voiced disapproval. Despite attempts to clarify its meaning, the slogan continues to generate controversy.

title: Congress has no blueprint, lying on caste census, says Rajnath Singh
summary: During Jharkhand rallies, defense minister Rajnath Singh accused Congress of misleading voters with promises of a caste census, highlighting their lack of a concrete implementation plan. Singh criticized Congress's history with the census, stating their failure to publish the 2011 report despite conducting it.

title: ED finds Rs 8.8 crore at Chennai office of Santiago Martin
summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) seized Rs 8.8 crore from the Chennai office of lottery tycoon Santiago Martin during searches related to a money laundering case. The investigation involves alleged illegal gains exceeding Rs 900 crore from lottery distribution and sales. The ED is investigating Martin and his associates for fraud in the distribution of Sikkim state lotteries.

title: Nepal's power starts flowing to Bangladesh through Indian grid
summary: India, Nepal, and Bangladesh launched their first trilateral power transaction, marking a significant step in regional energy cooperation. Nepal will export up to 40 MW of electricity to Bangladesh through the Indian grid, boosting sub-regional connectivity and supporting Bangladesh's energy needs. The agreement, signed last month, signifies a commitment to green energy initiatives and regional prosperity.

title: Jharkhand women's turnout at 69% against men's 64%
summary: Jharkhand's first phase of assembly elections saw a 66.6% voter turnout, with women exceeding men's participation by 4.7 percentage points. While the INDIA bloc attributed this to the success of welfare schemes like the Maiyya Samman Yojana, the BJP viewed it as a sign of discontent against the incumbent government.

title: In Dantewada, dreams of liquid gold turn to dust
summary: Residents in a cluster of villages in Dantewada, India, were astonished to discover petrol in their wells. The source was traced to a leak from a nearby fuel pump's underground reservoir. Authorities swiftly responded, sealing off the area and cutting off power to prevent a potential disaster. An investigation is underway.

title: Can't block religious place due to opposition by another group: Kerala high court
summary: The Kerala high court ruled that opposition from other groups shouldn't prevent the establishment of religious places in a democratic nation. The court made this decision while reviewing a Kozhikode collector's order that denied permission to operate a Muslim prayer hall due to opposition from people of other faiths.

title: 'Teaching not up to mark', CBSE plans big push to fill learning gaps
summary: To address learning gaps and ineffective teaching, CBSE is launching an 'assessment centre' by June 2024. The centre will provide teachers with tools to design effective assessments, track student progress, and improve teaching practices. CBSE will also introduce a reward system for teachers who develop high-quality assessment items.

These booklets, described as promoting rape culture, encourage students to view women as sexual objects and normalize the objectification and abuse of women, including their classmates and nurses.

title: Protests rock Manipur, homes of CM kin & ministers attacked
summary: Violence erupted in Manipur's Imphal valley after the discovery of six bodies, believed to be Meitei villagers, in the Barak river. Protesters, alleging inaction by authorities, targeted homes of ministers and MLAs. The incident follows the recent killing of 10 Hmar men by security forces, a clash that further inflamed ethnic tensions.

title: PM Modi arrives in Nigeria’s capital Abuja, receives grand welcome on historic visit
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Abuja, Nigeria, on Sunday, marking the first visit by an Indian prime minister to the West African nation in 17 years. The visit is part of a three-nation tour aimed at strengthening India's global partnerships. He received a ceremonial welcome and the "Key to the City" of Abuja.

The school administration, however, clarified that the structure was an unauthorized construction by a contractor and was being dismantled.

India to send 20-ton humanitarian aid package to flood-hit Nigeria: PM Modi
summary: During his visit to Nigeria, Indian Prime Minister Modi announced a 20-ton humanitarian aid package to support flood relief efforts. The aid will assist over 1.2 million people affected by the devastating floods that claimed the lives of over 300 people. Modi expressed condolences and highlighted the strong strategic partnership between India and Nigeria.

title: 'Congress finally acknowledging Balasaheb Thackeray's legacy': Milind Deora
summary: Congress MP Milind Deora welcomed Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's acknowledgment of Bal Thackeray's legacy, stating he had proposed a national day of mourning for the Shiv Sena founder in 2012. Gandhi, during her Maharashtra campaign, criticized the ruling alliance for disrespecting Shivaji Maharaj, highlighting the collapse of his statue and the removal of another from Parliament.

summary: Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge criticized Prime Minister Modi's silence on the escalating violence in Manipur, alleging a failure to address the unrest and accusing the BJP of using the situation for political gain. summary: A food van near Delhi's Vishwavidyalaya metro station caught fire on Sunday morning, sending plumes of black smoke into the air. The Delhi Fire Services extinguished the blaze, which broke out around 10:55 am, by noon. No injuries were reported. Police suspect an electrical fault in the cooking equipment caused the fire.

title: Manipur unrest: Amit Shah holds key meet with top officials amid fresh violence
summary: Union home minister Amit Shah reviewed the security situation in Manipur on Sunday after fresh violence erupted. He directed officials to take all necessary steps to restore peace. The unrest, marked by attacks on legislators' homes and killings in Jiribam, follows ethnic strife since May 2023, which has left over 220 dead and thousands displaced.

summary: The Chhattisgarh Waqf board has directed all mosques to seek approval for the topic of sermons delivered every Friday. This decision, aimed at preventing political agendas in mosques, requires Mutawallis (caretakers) to submit their sermon topics for approval, ensuring that mosques remain places of worship and not political platforms.

title: Eyeing 'office of profit' tweaks, Centre seeks to replace 1959 law
summary: Law ministry has drafted legislation to modernize the definition of 'offices of profit,' aiming to prevent the disqualification of Members of Parliament. The bill incorporates recommendations from a parliamentary committee, suggesting exemptions for MPs involved in key government programs like Swachh Bharat Mission and Smart City Mission.

title: Ahead of Maharashtra, Delhi polls, Centre & city gas companies spar over CNG price
summary: The oil ministry and city gas operators are at odds over CNG price hikes. Operators, facing reduced legacy gas allocations and higher import costs, want to raise prices. However, the government, citing operators' healthy profit margins, finds the proposal politically sensitive ahead of assembly polls.

title: Amid global race, India tests its first hypersonic missile
summary: India successfully test-fired its first hypersonic missile, achieving a speed exceeding five times the speed of sound. The missile, capable of carrying various payloads over 1,500km, marks a significant advancement in India's defense capabilities, positioning the nation among a select group with hypersonic technology.

title: 'Biren Singh failed': NPP withdraws support to BJP government in Manipur
summary: Meghalaya's ruling NPP withdrew support from the BJP-led Manipur government, citing chief minister Biren Singh's failure to curb the ongoing violence. NPP's withdrawal doesn't impact BJP's majority. Former CM Okram Ibobi Singh demanded Prime Minister Modi's intervention, threatening mass resignations by non-NDA MLAs if the situation doesn't improve.

title: House panel on OBCs likely to push for 'equivalence of posts'
summary: A parliamentary panel is urging the Indian government to address issues with the "creamy layer" policy for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). The panel highlights the lack of consistent "equivalence of posts" across government institutions, leading to discrepancies in how the policy is applied. They argue that the current system disadvantages OBC candidates from certain backgrounds and contradicts existing guidelines.

summary: The Supreme Court has rebuked the Delhi government for delaying the implementation of stricter pollution control measures, ordering that GRAP Stage 4 remain in effect regardless of AQI fluctuations. summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, during a Jharkhand rally, hinted at pursuing the construction of a Krishna temple in Mathura after the Ram Mandir inauguration. He heavily criticized the ruling JMM-led coalition, accusing them of corruption, illegal mining, and fostering infiltration. Adityanath pledged to recover looted funds, provide jobs, and expel infiltrators if the NDA comes to power.

summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh is slated to meet his Chinese counterpart, Dong Jun, during the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus in Laos. India highlighted Pakistan's denial of Azhar's presence despite his involvement in attacks like the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2001 Parliament attack. Azhar, designated a global terrorist, has long-standing ties with Pakistani intelligence.

summary: Eight lives were lost and 40 injured when a Lucknow-Delhi bus collided with a tanker on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh. The Prime Minister announced ₹2 lakh ex-gratia for deceased families and Rs 50,000 for the injured. Survivors allege driver fatigue caused the crash. A minister passing by oversaw rescue efforts and an investigation is underway.

summary: Defects plague the Delhi-Dausa stretch of the Mumbai Expressway, prompting an investigation by IIT experts. Quality issues in the top layer necessitate relaying within three months. Four contractors face blacklisting, and officials will be held accountable. The expressway, built using new technology, requires contractors to fix defects for ten years.

summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar expressed confidence in continued US support for the Quad under the second Trump administration. He highlighted Trump's role in revitalizing the alliance and its growth since 2017, emphasizing its equitable burden-sharing model. summary: Consumer Affairs Secretary Nidhi Khare urged the gems and jewellery industry to transparently disclose the nature of diamonds (natural or lab-grown) in sales and advertisements. summary: Trinamool Congress MP Saket Gokhale advocated for laws to address toxic work culture in the private sector, citing the death of a 26-year-old woman due to work pressure. Govt asks Meta to tackle cyber frauds on WhatsApp
summary: The Indian government has raised concerns with Meta regarding the increasing use of WhatsApp for online fraud. The IT Ministry has urged Meta to implement stronger measures to combat these scams, which have cost victims thousands of crores of rupees. Meta claims to be using AI and other technologies to address the issue and is cooperating with law enforcement.

summary: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the Ashtalakshmi Mahotsav, celebrating the northeastern states' culture. He criticized past governments for neglecting the region due to its lower population, emphasizing his government's commitment with increased ministerial visits and development initiatives. Modi highlighted the northeast's growing importance in India's growth story, predicting it will become a major hub.

title: Draft rules moot coaching centre infrastructure boost, SC seeks states' reply
summary: The Supreme Court has drafted model rules for coaching centers, emphasizing safety measures like fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, sprinkler systems, and flood prevention. The rules also mandate student counselors, helplines, grievance cells, ICCs, medical facilities, proper lighting and ventilation, safe drinking water, CCTV, and separate toilets. States are reviewing the proposed rules.

title: ED quizzing ex-official whole night in Chhattisgarh liquor case 'terrible': SC
summary: The Supreme Court criticized the Enforcement Directorate's overnight interrogation and 4 a.m. arrest of ex-IAS officer Anil Tuteja in the Chhattisgarh liquor scam as "terrible" and "disturbing." While upholding the arrest, the Court permitted Tuteja to seek bail. The ED, facing scrutiny for its methods, issued an internal circular curbing late-night interrogations following the incident.

title: PIL flags job threat to private companies' ICC members
summary: The Supreme Court is examining a PIL alleging retaliatory actions against Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) members in private companies who rule against senior management in sexual harassment cases. The petitioners argue that ICC members need protection and job security to ensure fair decisions without fear of reprisal, similar to the protections afforded to judges.

title: After giving birth, woman dies as hospital lift belt snaps
summary: An Armyman's wife died in Meerut after a hospital lift malfunctioned and crashed following her delivery. The woman suffered fatal head and neck injuries. The hospital has been sealed and its license revoked. Police have filed a culpable homicide case against the hospital owner, doctor, and staff.

title: Irked by 'simple' invite, Himachal Pradesh governor skips civic body Ambedkar event
summary: Himachal Pradesh Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla boycotted an event commemorating Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's death anniversary due to perceived disrespect in the invitation. Shukla stated he wasn't contacted personally by officials and the invitation listed the Chief Minister as the chief guest, prompting him to pay tribute at Raj Bhawan instead.

title: Northeast ignored for years, our government reversed trend: PM Modi
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the Northeast's development progress, emphasizing a shift from vote-centric politics to infrastructure investment, social initiatives, and peace-building. Reduced violence, historic peace agreements, and over Rs 5 lakh crore investment in the past decade showcase the region's growing importance in India's future, with improved connectivity and a focus on its cultural and economic strengths.

One teacher, Junaid Ahmed, suffered multiple stab wounds and is in critical condition. The other teacher sustained a minor hand injury. The student fled the scene and is currently being sought by police.

summary: A 17-year-old student fatally shot his school principal, Surendra Kumar Saxena, in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh. The student shot Saxena in the school washroom after being warned about his behavior. He then fled on the principal's scooter but was apprehended near the Uttar Pradesh border, still possessing the pistol. Police are investigating how the student obtained the firearm.

summary: Agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan assured farmers of guaranteed Minimum Support Price (MSP) purchases for all marketable surplus produce. This follows Rahul Gandhi's call for immediate implementation of farmers' demands, including a legal MSP guarantee. Chouhan emphasized the government's commitment to setting MSP at over 50% of production costs and expanding procurement beyond key crops like paddy and wheat.

summary: The Indian government revealed that 519 of its citizens were deported from the US between November 2023 and October 2024. The US government carried out these deportations via commercial and chartered flights because the individuals were deemed unauthorized to stay by US authorities.

summary: India continues to press for a fair and transparent legal process for religious leader Chinmoy Krishna Das, arrested in Bangladesh on sedition charges. summary: The UN General Assembly declared December 21st as World Meditation Day, led by a group of nations including India. The date coincides with the Winter Solstice and falls six months after International Yoga Day. The resolution aims to promote meditation for well-being and peace, particularly amidst global tensions, reflecting India's philosophy of global unity.

title: India to raise delay in S-400 missile systems & spares during Rajnath's visit to Russia
summary: India will address the delayed delivery of S-400 missile systems and spare parts during Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's visit to Russia. He will also commission the first of two stealth frigates being built there. Discussions will cover strengthening defence collaboration and reviewing ongoing military projects, including the delayed S-400 deliveries and a leased nuclear submarine.

This marks the first such statue in the nine states under the Seattle Indian Consulate's jurisdiction, honouring Gandhi's legacy of peace and non-violence.

summary: Sam Pitroda, Chairperson of the Indian Overseas Congress, reported repeated hacking of his laptop, smartphone, and server. Hackers demanded tens of thousands of dollars in cryptocurrency, threatening a smear campaign if unpaid. He cautioned his network against opening suspicious emails or messages, and plans to upgrade his security upon returning to Chicago.

summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar highlighted India's diplomatic efforts in mediating the Russia-Ukraine conflict and addressing global tensions. summary: Rahul Gandhi criticized the government for increasing income tax and GST rates for the common man while providing concessions to billionaires. He highlighted the proposed GST slab increase on daily necessities, including clothing, amidst rising inflation and unemployment. Gandhi pledged to oppose these measures and fight against the perceived injustice.

title: 'Remorseless, psychopath': How a class 12 student killed his school principal in Madhya Pradesh
summary: A 17-year-old student in Madhya Pradesh, India, fatally shot his school principal, Surendra Kumar Saxena, after being reprimanded for his behavior. The student, described by police as remorseless and possibly psychopathic, used a locally-made pistol and fled on the principal's scooter with a classmate. He was later apprehended near the Uttar Pradesh border.

title: BJP stands firm on Congress-Soros links, rejects calls for apology
summary: The BJP has accused the Congress party of collaborating with George Soros and his affiliated organizations to spread misinformation and disrupt Parliament. summary: The Supreme Court will address challenges to the Places of Worship Act, which prevents legal disputes aiming to alter the religious nature of sites established during independence. Several Hindus have filed lawsuits claiming mosques were originally temples, despite a previous Supreme Court ruling upholding the Act's secularism protection.

title: Maoists kill Bijapur woman in front of kin
summary: In Bijapur, Maoists murdered a 45-year-old anganwadi worker, Laxmi Padam, accusing her of being a police informer. The mother of three was strangled in front of her family, marking the 63rd civilian death by Maoists in Bastar division this year. This is the first time in over six years a woman has been killed in Bastar under such accusations.

summary: The US has rejected BJP's allegations of a "deep state" conspiracy involving the State Department, OCCRP, and George Soros to destabilize India by targeting PM Modi and Gautam Adani. summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's offer to lead the INDIA alliance has been met with silence from the Congress party. Congress sources suggest Banerjee's statement is viewed as political posturing amid internal party challenges and a perceived power struggle with her nephew. The Congress, not a TMC ally in West Bengal, sees no immediate threat from Banerjee's remarks.

summary: Farmer organizations met with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Saturday, urging GST exemption on agricultural inputs like equipment, feed, fertilizers, seeds, and medicines. The session will include MLA oath-taking, Speaker elections, the governor's address, budget presentation, and debates. The ruling alliance, led by Chief Minister Hemant Soren, aims to address opposition questions based on the previous government's achievements and has endorsed Rabindra Nath Mahato for Speaker.

summary: The AAP accused the BJP of hypocritically settling Rohingya refugees in Delhi while publicly condemning them, citing a tweet by Union Minister Hardeep Puri. The BJP retorted that the real issue is the presence of millions of illegal Rohingya and Bangladeshi immigrants across India, not legal refugees, and accused the AAP of deflecting from core issues.

summary: Home Minister Amit Shah announced a new laser-equipped anti-drone system is proving effective, neutralizing 55% of drones along the Punjab border, up from 3%. summary: Maoists in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur killed a second woman in two days, accusing her of being a police informant. summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court affirmed the Haryana government's authority to regulate mobile tower installations and impose fees. The court upheld the government's 2012 notification and rules, confirming its legislative power in this domain, while leaving the fee amount's validity to a separate bench.

title: Myanmar border fencing gathers pace, BRO to complete project in 10 years
summary: India is constructing a 1,643-km fence along its border with Myanmar to address security concerns, smuggling, and human trafficking. The $3.1 billion project, slated for completion within 10 years, includes provisions for controlled cross-border movement through biometric-enabled gates. While some local communities oppose the fence, authorities emphasize its necessity for national security and regulated trade.

summary: Three BNP-affiliated organizations in Dhaka protested against an attack on Bangladesh's diplomatic mission in India and alleged attempts to incite communal unrest. They submitted a memorandum to the Indian High Commission, with a senior BNP member warning of resistance against perceived Indian aggression. Concurrently, Bangladesh's home ministry ordered undocumented foreign nationals to legalize their status.

summary: Two policemen were found dead with gunshot wounds inside a police van in Udhampur, Jammu and Kashmir, on Sunday morning. A third officer in the vehicle survived the incident and is being questioned by authorities.

summary: Kerala police face a dilemma with 35 FIRs related to the Hema Committee report on sexual abuse in the Malayalam film industry. Actor Mala Parvathy has challenged the probe in the Supreme Court, while a nodal officer has been appointed to support survivors facing threats.

summary: Bangladesh's foreign affairs adviser acknowledges a recent "stalemate" with India following reported attacks on Hindus. Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri's visit marks the first high-level interaction since Bangladesh's interim government took power.

summary: Following opposition allegations of EVM manipulation in the recent Maharashtra assembly elections, Nanded district officials conducted a post-election verification. The verification of 75 polling centers revealed no discrepancies between EVMs and VVPAT slips. The BJP-led alliance swept all nine constituencies in Nanded, prompting the opposition's concerns.

title: ‘What is sauce for goose ought to be sauce for gander’: SC grants relief to woman army officer, orders permanent commission
summary: The Supreme Court granted permanent commission to a woman Army officer, rectifying her wrongful exclusion from consideration. India remains concerned about regional stability given Syria's proximity to key Gulf partners.

summary: Telangana High Court revoked ex-BRS MLA Chennamaneni Ramesh's Indian citizenship, deeming him a German citizen. He was fined ₹30 lakh for concealing this and misleading the court. summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee downplayed threats from Bangladeshi figures to occupy Indian states, attributing them to illness. title: Deploy paramilitary forces for WB co-operative bank polls: SC
summary: The Supreme Court ordered central forces deployment for the December 31 Contai Cooperative Bank elections in West Bengal's Nandigram, following allegations of electoral roll irregularities and polling booth relocation to communally sensitive areas. title: CM unveils Telangana 'mother' statue, says bid to alter it will invite action
summary: Telangana CM A Revanth Reddy unveiled the official Telangana Thalli statue, warning against any alterations or insults to it.
